ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The five small shaded squares inside this unit square are congruent and have disjoint interiors. The midpoint of each side of the middle square coincides with one of the vertices of the other four small squares as shown. The common side length is $\frac{a-\sqrt{2}}{b}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers. What is $a+b$ ?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an outer unit square, and inside there are five gray small squares. Four gray small squares are respectively attached to the four corners of the unit square, with sides parallel to the outer square; in the middle there is also a gray square of the same size, rotated into a diamond shape. The vertices of the small squares at the four corners that are close to the center respectively coincide with the midpoints of the four sides of the middle diamond square, and the white region in the figure forms a cross-shaped gap. Reasoning: Let the common side length of the five congruent small squares be s. The squares at the four corners each occupy a length s on the side of the outer unit square, so their four vertices close to the center form an axis-aligned small square whose side length is 1 - 2s. According to the problem statement and the image, these four vertices are exactly the midpoints of the four sides of the middle square. For a square with side length s, the side length of the square obtained by connecting the midpoints of the four sides is s/√2. Therefore there is the equation 1 - 2s = s/√2. Solving gives s = 1/(2 + 1/√2) = (4 - √2)/7. Therefore a = 4, b = 7, a + b = 11.

Let the common side length be s. The inner vertices of the four corner squares form a smaller axis-aligned square whose side length is 1 - 2s, since each corner square removes length s from each end of a side of the unit square. From the text and diagram, these four inner vertices are exactly the midpoints of the four sides of the middle square. For any square of side s, the square formed by joining the four side midpoints has side length s/√2. Therefore 1 - 2s = s/√2. Solve to get s = 1/(2 + 1/√2) = (4 - √2)/7. Thus a = 4 and b = 7, so a + b = 11.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram locally: the top-left shaded corner square has side length s, and its lower-right vertex lies on the upper-left side of the central diamond as that side's midpoint. By symmetry visible in the diagram, the top vertex of the central diamond lies on the vertical midline of the unit square, so its horizontal coordinate is 1/2, while the lower-right vertex of the top-left corner square is horizontally s from the left side. Thus the horizontal distance from that midpoint to the top vertex of the diamond is 1/2 - s. Since this segment is half a side of the middle square, its length is s/2; because the central square is drawn as a 45-degree diamond, the horizontal component of this half-side is (s/2)/√2 = s/(2√2). In the top-left part of the diagram, the lower-right vertex of the top-left shaded square lies on the upper-left side of the central diamond, at the midpoint of that side. The whole configuration is symmetric about the vertical midline of the unit square, so the top vertex of the central diamond lies on the vertical line x = 1/2.

Reasoning: Let the common side length of each shaded square be s. The top-left corner square has side length s and is flush with the left side of the unit square, so its lower-right vertex has horizontal coordinate s. The top vertex of the central diamond has horizontal coordinate 1/2. Therefore, the horizontal distance from the midpoint point on the upper-left side of the diamond to the top vertex of the diamond is 1/2 - s.

Since the central diamond is also a square of side length s, the distance from the midpoint of one side to an adjacent vertex along that side is s/2. The side of the central square is drawn at a 45-degree angle, so the horizontal component of this half-side segment is (s/2)/sqrt(2) = s/(2sqrt(2)). Thus 1/2 - s = s/(2sqrt(2)).

Solving: 1 - 2s = s/sqrt(2), so 1 = s(2 + 1/sqrt(2)). Hence s = 1/(2 + 1/sqrt(2)) = 2/(4 + sqrt(2)) = (4 - sqrt(2))/7. Therefore a = 4 and b = 7, so a + b = 11.

claims.claim: The squares at the four corners each occupy a length s on the side of the outer unit square.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The squares at the four corners each occupy a length s on the side of the outer unit square

claims.claim: The four vertices of the small squares at the four corners that are close to the center form an axis-aligned small square.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore their four vertices close to the center form an axis-aligned small square

claims.claim: The side length of this axis-aligned small square is 1 - 2s.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Its side length is 1 - 2s

claims.claim: For a square with side length s, the side length of the square obtained by connecting the midpoints of the four sides is s/√2.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: For a square with side length s, the side length of the square obtained by connecting the midpoints of the four sides is s/√2

claims.claim: From the above side-length relationship, the equation 1 - 2s = s/√2 is obtained.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore there is the equation 1 - 2s = s/√2

claims.claim: Solving the equation gives s = 1/(2 + 1/√2) = (4 - √2)/7.
claims.label: reasoning
